why: Both analyses land on the same lowest-cost-per-ton, culture-plus-technology hedgehog and cover all the key brutal facts with comparable flagging of assumptions. Analysis 2 explicitly recognises the company as already great and frames its stop-doing list as temptations to refuse (no diversification, no old-mill purchases, no added layers, no touching bonuses or no-layoff, iron carbide contained), whereas Analysis 1 rates it only 'clearly good' and leans toward governance and bonus changes.
